test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the most logical sequence of sentences from the options to construct a meaningful and cohesive paragraph.

a. Researchers from five medical centres around the country found that insomniacs were also significantly likely to have poor health, such as chest pain, arthritis, and depression, as well as difficulties doing daily duties.

b. Even temporary sleep loss can disrupt the body's capacity to break down carbohydrates, interfere with hormones, and aggravate diabetes and high blood pressure.

c. So, make time for whatever helps you sleep, whether it's exercise, massages, yoga, meditation, or a fragrance bath.

d. Sleep deprivation has frightening consequences for many biological processes.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option (1)** i.e. **d, a, b, c**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The paragraph begins with **part (d)**, discussing the consequences of sleep deprivation and setting the tone for the importance of sleep.
 
• Following that, **part (a)** provides findings from medical research that link insomnia to poor health, further highlighting the importance of sleep.
 
• **Part (b)** explains how even temporary sleep loss can disrupt various biological processes, which emphasizes the severity of sleep deprivation.
 
• **Part (c)** concludes by offering solutions to improve sleep, suggesting ways to prioritize sleep for better health and well-being.

Therefore, the correct answer is **d, a, b, c.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 (d, a, c, b):** This option starts with solutions for better sleep in **part (c)** before discussing the consequences of sleep deprivation, which interrupts the natural flow of information.
 
• **Option 3 (d, c, a, b):** By beginning with solutions in **part (c)** and jumping straight into health findings in **part (a)**, this option disrupts the progression from the problem (sleep deprivation) to the solution (better sleep). 
 
• **Option 4 (d, c, b, a):** This option introduces solutions in **part (c)** too early in the sequence, breaking the logical order from the causes and effects of sleep deprivation.
